memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses then wrote down everything the Lord had said. He got up early the next morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up twelve stone pillars representing the twelve tribes of Israel." - Exodus 24:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses does something simple but significant: he writes it all down. God's words were not left to fade in the people's memory or drift with each retelling. They were recorded, fixed, preserved. Then Moses built an altar and set up twelve pillars, one for each tribe — a visible, physical reminder that every tribe stood together in this covenant with God.

There is real wisdom here. We are forgetful people. What moves us deeply today can slip from our minds within weeks. That is why God gave His people a written word rather than leaving them to rely on impressions and memories. And it is why we hold Scripture so dearly — it is God's Word preserved, unchanging, available to us long after the feelings of a moment have faded.

The twelve pillars remind us of something too: God deals with a people, not just isolated individuals. Every tribe had its stone. No one was left out or forgotten. In Christ, we are likewise built together as one people, living stones formed into a spiritual house (1 Pet 2:5). Your faith is personal, but it was never meant to be solitary. Ground yourself in God's written Word, and root yourself among God's gathered people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I grounding my faith in God's written Word rather than passing feelings?
Do I see myself as part of God's people, not merely an isolated believer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for preserving Your Word so I need not rely on fading memory. Root me deeply in Scripture and knit me closely to Your people. Amen.
